scheme_name: National Centre of Excellence for Green Port & Shipping (NCoEGPS)
overview: The National Centre of Excellence for Green Port & Shipping (NCoEGPS) is an initiative under the Sagarmala Programme aimed at promoting innovation, research, and development in green technologies for ports and shipping. It focuses on reducing carbon emissions, enhancing energy efficiency, and supporting sustainable practices in maritime operations. The Centre serves as a hub for collaboration between industry, academia, and government to advance green port and shipping solutions across India.
objectives: Promote research and innovation in green port and shipping technologies
Support development of low-carbon and energy-efficient solutions for maritime sector
Facilitate collaboration between industry, academia, and government stakeholders
Provide incubation and testing support for green technologies in ports and shipping
Advance policy and regulatory frameworks for sustainable port operations
Enhance skill development and capacity building in green maritime practices
eligibility: Entities engaged in innovation, research, or development of green technologies for ports and shipping, including startups, MSMEs, research institutions, and industry players, are eligible to engage with the National Centre of Excellence for Green Port & Shipping (NCoEGPS).
benefits: Access to research infrastructure, testing facilities, mentorship, technical guidance, collaboration opportunities with industry and government, policy advocacy support, and visibility in national green maritime initiatives.
financial_support: The Centre provides support through grants, subsidies, or in-kind assistance for eligible projects, though specific quantum and disbursement mechanisms are not detailed in the available evidence.
application_process: 1. Identify relevant green port or shipping innovation project aligned with NCoEGPS objectives. 2. Prepare project proposal detailing innovation, sustainability impact, and implementation plan. 3. Submit proposal through the designated channel or portal associated with the Sagarmala Programme. 4. Undergo technical and feasibility review by the Centre’s expert panel. 5. Receive approval and access to support mechanisms including mentorship, testing, or funding as applicable.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
caveats: Support is subject to availability of resources and alignment with Centre’s strategic priorities
Financial support, if any, is discretionary and based on project evaluation
Continued engagement may require periodic progress reporting and outcomes demonstration
